narrative.coaching_note: Clean your hands right after touching the patient zone before touching anything outside it. You touched bed rail A with your bare hand starting at 0.5 seconds, and then you touched phone at 6.6 seconds, which carried MRSA from bed rail A to phone. You missed hand hygiene for Moment 5 at 4.7 seconds after that contact with bed rail A. Later you put on a glove at 10.9 seconds, touched bed rail A with your gloved hand at 11.1 seconds, and then touched call button at 16.4 seconds, which carried contamination to call button. You missed hand hygiene for Moment 5 at 18.7 seconds after touching call button. Cleaning hands and changing how you use gloves after the patient zone keeps MRSA from moving to shared items like phone.
narrative.audit_summary: The source was bed rail A. Bare hand contacted bed rail A at 0.5-2.3s and 4.2-4.7s, then phone at 6.6-9.9s. After glove donning at 10.9s, gloved hand contacted bed rail A at 11.1-14.3s, call button at 16.4-18.7s, phone at 19.3-22.5s, and bed rail A at 22.9-24.7s. Transfers modeled: bed rail A to bare hand at 0.5s, bare hand to phone at 6.6s, bed rail A to gloved hand at 11.1s, gloved hand to call button at 16.4s. Two Moment 5 opportunities missed at 4.7s (bare hand) and 18.7s (gloved hand). No resident exposures. End contamination included bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A, call button, and phone. For MRSA, alcohol rub and soap and water are effective.
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was hand hygiene for Moment 5 at 4.7 seconds.
